name: Diving Deep into Sialadenitis and Sialadenosis: Symptoms, Diagnosis, and Therapeutic Approaches

sections.overview:
Diving Deep into Sialadenitis and Sialadenosis: Symptoms, Diagnosis, and Therapeutic Approaches 

 Abstract 
 Sialadentitis and Sialadenosis are among the commonest reasons for swelling of the submandibular gland. There are mild differences between both the conditions. Sialadentitis is an inflammatory condition of the salivary gland, usually due to viral or bacterial infections, whereas Sialadenosis is a non-inflammatory condition that affects the parotid or the submandibular gland. 
Sialadentitis of the parotid gland is commoner than that of submandibular gland. To know the disease better we need to know the anatomy and physiology of the salivary gland. Salivary gland consists of – sublingual, submandibular and parotid gland. Among these three parotid glands is the largest one due to which it is more prone to diseases. Commonly disorders of salivary glands are due to pathology of any of these glands.
sections.introduction:
Both the two diseases Sialadentitis and Sialadenosis are the disorders of the salivary gland. Major functions of salivary glands are that it maintains our oral health and also the overall health. It also helps keep cavities away and lubrication to the food we chew hence helps in better digestion too. Hence pathologies in this part can cause a lot of disorders in the overall functioning of the body. 
 Sialadentitis – Sialadentitis is the commonest cause of acute salivary gland infection that may be caused due to various types of infection like bacterial, fungal or viral. Sialadentitis is the inflammation of the submandibular gland that can result from dryness of the mouth due to salivary stone, inadequate consumption of fluid and many others. 
 Sialadenosis – Sialadenosis on the other hand is a non inflammatory condition mainly of the parotid gland and very rarely the submandibular gland due to any other systemic disease. It is a chronic condition, and can be painless.
sections.causes_of_sialadentitis:
Infections (Viral, bacterial of Fungal) 
 Dehydration due to less intake of fluid or intake of diuretics 
 Poor oral hygiene 
 Malnutrition 
 Medications (antihistamines or diuretics)
sections.causes_of_sialadenosis:
Diabetes mellitus 
 Vitamin deficiency 
 Malabsorption 
 Autoimmune disorders 
 Hypothyroidism 
 Liver cirrhosis
sections.sign_and_symptoms_of_sialadentitis_inclu:
Enlargement and tenderness of salivary gland 
 Difficulty in swallowing and eating 
 Pain and swelling in mouth 
 Fever with chills 
 Dryness of mouth 
 Lower secretion of saliva than usual 
 Foul taste in mouth 
 Swelling seen in nearby regions like neck and cheeks
sections.signs_and_symptoms_of_sialadenosis_inclu:
Painless 
 Lower secretion of saliva than usual 
 Tenderness 
 Bilateral Enlargement parotid gland
sections.diagnosis_of_sialadenitis_and_sialadenos:
Physical examinations – History taking of patient 
 X-Ray to check for inflammation 
 CT scan (Computerised Tomography) – to rule out sialolith 
 MRI (Magnetic resonance imaging) – to check for nay malignancies 
 CBC (Complete Blood Count) 
 Salivary gland scan
sections.treatment_of_sialadenitis_and_sialadenos:
Reestablishment of hydration of the patient 
 Administration of antibiotics may be required 
 Massage of salivary gland or heat compressions may be effective 
 Surgical removal can be done
sections.complications_of_sialadentitis_and_siala:

 Formation of abscess (most serious of all) 
 Tooth decay 



 Ayurvedic Aspect Of Sialadenitis And Sialadenosis 
 In Ayurveda these diseases are considered among mukha rogas that are 65 in numbers. that are diseases of the mouth or the buccal cavity. Achrya Sushruta says that these mukha rogas are due to alteration of the three doshas Vata, Pitta and Kapha as just like the functioning of entire body these three doshas also plays an important role in the functioning of mukha i.e the mouth. Vitiation of vata and kapha dosha causes pain and inflammation of the salivary gland. These vitiation of doshas are due to poor lifestyle and other ill dietary choices. Not maintaining required dental hygiene also plays an important role.
